chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"The judges are four: three in the Hellfire and one in Paradise. A man who judges with injustice while knowing it is in the Hellfire; and a man who judges with injustice while not knowing that he is judging with injustice, he is in the Hellfire; and a man who judges with the truth while not knowing it is the truth, he is in the Hellfire; and a man who judges with the truth while knowing it is the truth, he is in Paradise."

And he (peace be upon him) said: "Judgment is of two types: the judgment of Allah, Exalted and Mighty, and the judgment of Ignorance (al-Jahiliyyah). So whoever errs from the judgment of Allah, he has judged with the judgment of Ignorance."

key_terms.الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: Ignorance (pre-Islamic era concept applied to judgment)

ai.seo_question: What are the four types of judges according to Shia hadith and their ultimate fate?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to establish the epistemological criteria for judicial validity, emphasizing that mere correctness is insufficient without conscious awareness of the truth. The classification highlights that ignorance negates reward even in just rulings, while conscious deviation or error leads to punishment, reinforcing the concept of *Hukm al-Jahiliyyah* (Judgment of Ignorance) as the antithesis of divine law. This hadith serves as a foundational text for Shia jurisprudence regarding the qualifications and spiritual accountability of *Qudat* (judges).
